contract: Pure ALLOW/ASK/DENY reducer over typed exact-match rules (effect class, principal, tenant, resource, payload, target, field, write value) with deny > ask > allow, default deny, whole-action escrow on ASK, and whole-proposal rejection when writes exceed the trusted own authority or, for a child, the parent's authority. Trusted proposer and host-derived effect class come from context; proposal copies must match. Portable tagged value domain with duplicate-preserving records and fixed bounds; three failure classes (DENY, invalid_input, unavailable_context). Policy identity (id, version, content_hash) on every decision.
limits: No security certification, identity guarantee, authentication, principal service or policy-engine provider.
Selected laws hold with respect to Cure eq_write; its agreement with Elixir structural equality and its reflexivity are finite tests (pinned Cure keeps symbolic Int equality neutral).
Validation, normalization, bounds, the control-key DENY and proposer/effect-class mismatch are Elixir-side and test-grounded only.
No law states that decide's verdict equals join_all of its per-write rule verdicts; that composition is by construction and tested.
Authority is exact writes, one value per (target, field); the host builds exact-value authority per action. No wildcard or range authority.
One requirement per ASK; several distinct requirements fail closed. Multi-approver needs a new Piece ID.
The host supplies the policy SHA-256; the Piece compares it and does not authenticate its origin. External decoders must reject duplicate keys.
Every gated effect must be at least one typed write; an empty write set is rejected.

grounding.claim: join(Deny, v) = Deny for every verdict v.
join(v, Deny) = Deny for every verdict v (exhaustive).
join(Ask, Allow) = Ask.
join(Allow, Ask) = Ask.
join is idempotent (exhaustive over the 3 verdicts).
join is commutative (exhaustive).
join is associative (exhaustive).
For all verdict lists p, s: join_all(p ++ [Deny | s]) = Deny (induction on p). About join_all; decide applies join_all to its per-write verdicts by construction.
For all p, v, s: join(join_all(p ++ [v | s]), v) = join_all(p ++ [v | s]) (induction); the reduced verdict is at least every element.
finish(Ask, RequirementOne(q), ws, ...) escrows exactly ws.
finish(Ask, any choice, ws, ...) permits no writes.
finish(Deny, ...) permits no writes.
finish(Deny, ...) escrows no writes.
finish(Allow, ...) escrows no writes.
The authority-exceeded decision escrows no writes.
For all policy, action, own, parent: subset(permitted_of(decide(...)), own) = True, subset with respect to eq_write.
For all policy, action, own, parent: subset(escrowed_of(decide(...)), own) = True, with respect to eq_write.
For all policy, action, own, p: subset(permitted_of(decide(policy, action, own, ParentAuthority(p))), p) = True, with respect to eq_write.
For all policy, action, own, p: escrowed writes of a child decision are a subset of p, with respect to eq_write.
If verdict_of(decide(...)) = Deny then escrowed_of(decide(...)) = [] (hypothesis form).

Pinned Cure checks the production reducer with a clean audit (no axioms, holes, opacity or unproven totality); every function is @total. Tests reject mutated DENY absorption, ASK permitting writes, skipped containment, text equal to bytes, and an unfinished law.

Listed scenarios: verdict precedence, default deny, rule conditions, forged proposer, mislabelled effect class, containment and child bound, exact-value authority, unavailable context, ambiguous requirement, control keys, pinned fault order, empty writes, model text, value validation, normalization, bounds at limit and limit + 1, Elixir/Cure equality agreement, proposer_view. Not universal proofs.
Relies on the pinned Cure compiler, kernel and audit.
Relies on pinned Elixir/OTP binary byte order, String.valid?/1 and term equality for normalization.

The host derives the trusted proposer identity, effect class and authority from its own authenticated state, supplies the policy artifact and its SHA-256, and serializes decisions with the state they guard.

telemetry.contract: Pure callable; the invoking Unit/Assembly instruments. Decisions are caller-retained records, not telemetry.

config.contract: Per call, no default, no hot reconfiguration: the trusted policy (schema and bounds as in the README, immutable per id/version/content_hash) and proposer_view disclosure (:full | :verdict_only). Bounds are fixed Contract constants.

control.contract: No lifecycle to pause, drain or resume.
